paragraphs.title: The Demand to Lighten the Burden and the Consultation

easy.explanation: Rehoboam went to Shechem, where all Israel had gathered to make him king.

easy.explanation: Jeroboam and all the congregation of Israel came and spoke unto Rehoboam.
easy.q: Who was called to speak with Rehoboam on behalf of the people?

easy.explanation: The people asked Rehoboam to make his father's heavy yoke and grievous service lighter.
easy.q: What did the people ask Rehoboam to do?

answers: His father had made their yoke grievous
Jeroboam had commanded them to ask
medium.explanation: They said that Rehoboam's father had made their yoke grievous and asked him to lighten it.
medium.q: Why did the people ask Rehoboam to lighten the burden?

answers: Depart for three days and return
medium.explanation: Rehoboam told them, “Depart yet for three days, then come again to me.”
medium.q: What did Rehoboam tell the people to do after hearing their request?

medium.explanation: The people wanted Rehoboam to reduce the hard service and heavy yoke imposed by Solomon.
medium.q: What does “make thou the grievous service of thy father ... lighter” mean?

answers: First from the old men, then from the young men
First from the young men, then from the people
He immediately sent the people away
challenge.explanation: Rehoboam first consulted the old men and then consulted the young men who had grown up with him.
challenge.q: In what order did Rehoboam seek advice?

answers: He wanted advice about how to answer the people
He had already decided to make war
He had given up the kingdom
challenge.explanation: He asked his advisers, “How do ye advise that I may answer this people?”
challenge.q: What does Rehoboam's consultation show about his immediate response?

answers: The old men had stood before Solomon, while the young men had grown up with Rehoboam
The old men were from Judah, while the young men were from Dan
The old men were priests, while the young men were warriors
challenge.explanation: The old men had stood before Solomon, while the young men had grown up with Rehoboam and stood before him.
challenge.q: What distinction does the passage make between the old men and the young men?

paragraphs.title: The Young Advisers and Rehoboam's Harsh Answer

easy.explanation: The young men advised Rehoboam to add to the people's yoke.
easy.q: What advice did the young men give Rehoboam?

easy.explanation: The king answered the people roughly.
easy.q: How did Rehoboam answer the people?

easy.explanation: Rehoboam said, “My father also chastised you with whips.”
easy.q: What did Rehoboam say his father had used to chastise the people?

answers: He was weaker than his father
His little finger was thicker than his father's loins
He did not want to reign
medium.explanation: They advised him to say, “My little finger shall be thicker than my father's loins.”
medium.q: What did the young men advise Rehoboam to say about his strength?

medium.explanation: Rehoboam followed their counsel and answered the people harshly.
medium.q: What resulted from Rehoboam following the young men's counsel?

answers: I will give you another city
medium.explanation: The phrase means that Rehoboam would make the people's burden heavier.
medium.q: What does “I will add to your yoke” mean?

answers: The old men advised serving the people, while the young men advised displaying power
The old men advised war, while the young men advised peace
The old men advised leaving, while the young men advised staying
challenge.explanation: The old men advised Rehoboam to serve the people and speak good words, but the young men advised him to increase their burden.
challenge.q: What was the main contrast between the counsel of the old men and that of the young men?

answers: It says the cause was from the Lord
It says Rehoboam rejected God's word
It does not mention the Lord
challenge.explanation: The passage says the king did not hearken to the people because “the cause was from the Lord.”
challenge.q: How does the passage connect Rehoboam's answer with God's word?

answers: A promise to make the burden lighter
A threat to increase the people's suffering
A request for the people to choose another king
challenge.explanation: The contrast between whips and scorpions expresses a threat of harsher treatment.
challenge.q: What do the images of whips and scorpions communicate?

answers: What portion have we in David?
We will all go up to Jerusalem

easy.q: What did the people say after Rehoboam would not hearken unto them?

easy.explanation: Rehoboam made speed to get up to his chariot and flee to Jerusalem.
easy.q: What did Rehoboam do after Adoram was killed?

easy.explanation: Israel called Jeroboam and made him king over all Israel.
easy.q: Whom did Israel make king over them?

medium.explanation: There was none that followed the house of David but the tribe of Judah only.
medium.q: Who remained with the house of David after the division?

answers: He was a priest at Bethel
medium.explanation: Rehoboam sent Adoram, who was over the tribute.
medium.q: What was Adoram's position?

answers: The people replied to and rejected the king
The people returned the king to Jerusalem
The people gave the king a gift
medium.explanation: The people answered Rehoboam with words rejecting the house of David.
medium.q: What does “the people answered the king” mean in this context?

answers: Rehoboam's refusal to hearken unto the people
challenge.explanation: After Rehoboam refused to listen, Israel rebelled against the house of David and made Jeroboam king.
challenge.q: What directly led Israel to make Jeroboam king?

answers: The people returned to their own places
The people went up to the temple
challenge.explanation: The phrase called the people to depart and return to their own homes or places.
challenge.q: What does “to your tents, O Israel” mean here?

answers: Israel separated from the house of David
challenge.explanation: Israel rebelled against the house of David, while Judah remained under Rehoboam.
challenge.q: What political change is described in these verses?

paragraphs.title: Preparation for War and Its Cancellation by the Prophet

easy.explanation: Rehoboam assembled all the house of Judah with the tribe of Benjamin.
easy.q: Which tribes did Rehoboam gather for war?

answers: To fight against the house of Israel
easy.explanation: He gathered the army to fight against Israel and bring the kingdom again to himself.
easy.q: Why did Rehoboam gather the army?

easy.explanation: Shemaiah delivered the word of the Lord to Rehoboam and the people.
easy.q: Who stopped the planned war?

answers: Do not fight against their brethren
medium.explanation: The Lord commanded them not to go up or fight against their brethren, the children of Israel.
medium.q: What did Shemaiah command Rehoboam and the people?

answers: The matter was from the Lord
medium.explanation: The Lord said, “For this thing is from me.”
medium.q: Why were they not to fight, according to the word of the Lord?

medium.explanation: Shemaiah called the children of Israel their brethren.
medium.q: Who were “your brethren” in the command, “fight against your brethren”?

answers: They obeyed the word of the Lord and returned home
challenge.explanation: They hearkened to the word of the Lord and returned according to his word.
challenge.q: How did Rehoboam and the people respond to Shemaiah's command?

answers: He intended to fight but returned home
He intended to flee but went to war
He intended to build a city but appointed priests
challenge.explanation: Rehoboam gathered an army for war, but the prophetic command caused him to abandon the attack.
challenge.q: What changed between Rehoboam's intention and his actual action?

answers: They were brothers from the same people
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that the two sides were still fellow Israelites and brothers.
challenge.q: What does the phrase “the children of Israel” emphasize about the opposing groups?

easy.explanation: Jeroboam built Shechem in mount Ephraim and dwelt there.
easy.q: What city did Jeroboam build in mount Ephraim?

answers: That the people would return to Rehoboam
That the people would leave Bethel

easy.q: What did Jeroboam fear?

answers: Their hearts might turn again to Rehoboam
medium.explanation: Jeroboam feared that worship at Jerusalem would turn the people back to Rehoboam.
medium.q: Why was Jeroboam afraid of the people going up to Jerusalem?

answers: It helped establish and strengthen his rule
medium.explanation: Building Shechem and Penuel was part of establishing Jeroboam's rule.
medium.q: How did building the cities relate to Jeroboam's kingdom?

answers: The kingdom might go back to David's royal house
The kingdom would be newly built
medium.explanation: Jeroboam feared that the kingdom would return to the rule of the house of David.
medium.q: What does “Now shall the kingdom return to the house of David” mean?

answers: Going to Jerusalem might cause the people's hearts to return to Rehoboam
Building Shechem would destroy the kingdom
Dwelling in Penuel would send the people to Egypt
challenge.explanation: Jeroboam connected pilgrimage to Jerusalem with the people's return to Rehoboam.
challenge.q: What cause-and-effect connection appears in Jeroboam's reasoning?

answers: He did not know Jerusalem existed
challenge.explanation: Jeroboam said that if the people returned to Rehoboam, they would kill him and restore Rehoboam.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Jeroboam's fear?

answers: As places connected with establishing Jeroboam's kingdom
As places where Rehoboam was crowned
As places where Shemaiah stopped the army
challenge.explanation: Jeroboam built both cities after becoming king over Israel.
challenge.q: How are Shechem and Penuel presented in the passage?

paragraphs.title: The Calves and an Alternative Cult

easy.explanation: Jeroboam made two calves of gold.
easy.q: How many golden calves did Jeroboam make?

easy.explanation: He set one calf in Bethel and the other in Dan.
easy.q: Where did Jeroboam place the calves?

answers: People from the lowest of the people, not sons of Levi
Sons of the house of David
easy.explanation: Jeroboam made priests of the lowest of the people, who were not sons of Levi.
easy.q: Who were the priests appointed by Jeroboam?

answers: To keep the people from going up to Jerusalem
To bring the people back to Rehoboam
To prepare the people for war
medium.explanation: Jeroboam wanted an alternative place of worship so the people would not go to Jerusalem.
medium.q: What was the purpose of placing the calves?

medium.explanation: He made an house of high places and appointed priests there.
medium.q: What else did Jeroboam make besides the calves?

answers: People chosen from among the ordinary people
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to people selected from among the people rather than from the tribe of Levi.
medium.q: What does “the lowest of the people” mean in this passage?

answers: With golden calves, high places, and priests who were not sons of Levi
challenge.explanation: Jeroboam combined the calves, the high places, and non-Levitical priests into an alternative system of worship.
challenge.q: How did Jeroboam create an alternative religious system?

answers: It was intended to prevent the people from returning to Rehoboam
It was intended to strengthen the house of David
It was intended to end the kingdom of Israel
challenge.explanation: The alternative worship was designed to keep the people from going to Jerusalem and returning to Rehoboam.
challenge.q: What was the connection between the alternative worship and Jeroboam's fear?

answers: They were not sons of Levi
They were all sons of David
challenge.explanation: The passage specifically says that Jeroboam's priests were not of the sons of Levi.
challenge.q: What detail distinguishes Jeroboam's priests from the priests expected under the law?

He received it from the old men

He returned to the house of David
